title: helm(private): values templating, init-hooks and upgrade/rollback enhancements for Private installer
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Stabilize the Redwood Private Helm chart values schema and templating to make in-place upgrades and rollbacks more reliable for on-prem/VPC installs. This PR addresses several upgrade/rollback failure modes we've observed in the field (missing init-job ordering, schema drift in values.yaml, and templating edge-cases with optional KMS and nodeSelector blocks).

What this PR does:
- Introduces a stricter values.schema.json for charts/private with clearer defaults and nullable/conditional fields for encryption, KMS, and tolerations.
- Reworks templating helpers (_helpers.tpl) to provide safe defaults and idempotent rendering for init hooks and post-upgrade probes.
- Adds an explicit init-job template (templates/init-job.yaml) with ownerReferences and deterministic backoff to avoid duplicate init jobs on retries.
- Adds pre-upgrade and post-rollback helm hook templates (templates/upgrade-hook.yaml, templates/rollback-hook.yaml) to orchestrate DB migrations and backup snapshots for Private's Postgres and stateful components. Hooks are optional and gated by values:enableHooks.
- Adds a small kustomize-friendly NOTES.txt and README documenting upgrade/rollback steps and recommended linear tasks to run before upgrades.
- Adds tests and CI jobs: helm linting, schema validation, and a targeted e2e that runs helm install -> helm upgrade -> helm rollback against a kind cluster image used by our CI.

Checklist (PR author):
- [x] values.schema.json updated and validated against current installer docs
- [x] Templating helpers updated with unit tests (helm-template snapshots)
- [x] Init job added and validated for idempotency
- [x] Hooks gated behind values flag and documented in README
- [x] CI e2e added to catch helm upgrade/rollback regressions

Testing performed:
- Local: helm template run with minimal and full values sets; schema validation with kubeval/jsonschema.
- CI: full lint + unit templating snapshot + e2e (install -> upgrade -> rollback) passing on Linux runners. One intermittent flake in the e2e (timing-sensitive probe) was addressed by adding a probeTimeout value and retry logic in the init-job.

Rollback story and operational notes:
- The rollback-hook triggers snapshot of Postgres before a failing upgrade when values.enableHooks=true. The hook is optional for air-gapped customers; disabled by default in the minimal profile.
- The init-job now uses deterministic labels/annotations so Helm identifies and reuses the same job across retries instead of creating duplicates.

Related: ENG-4128 (upgrade reliability), ENG-4187 (helm schema tightening). Further follow-ups: add a migration dry-run mode and a canary hook that pings Console for readiness before DNS switch.

Links: internal linear tasks (https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4128), reference runbook changes included in charts/private/README.md.

review_comments: Arjun Patel (2026-02-19): Question: for air-gapped customers we shouldn't require KMS defaults — can we ensure kms.* fields are fully optional? Response: made kms.* nullable and added clear docs in README.
Sofia Martinez (2026-02-20): Suggestion: add ownerReferences to init job so garbage collection behaves correctly on namespace delete. Response: added ownerReferences and unit-tested rendering.

Ethan Zhao (2026-02-21): CI flake on e2e — looks timing-related, can we expose probe timeout as value? Response: added values.initJob.probeTimeout and increased default backoff; reran CI and e2e passed.

release_notes:
- Stabilize Helm values schema for Private installer; make kms/encryption fields optional and nullable.
- Add idempotent init-job to prevent duplicate jobs during retries.
- Add optional pre-upgrade and post-rollback hooks (gated by values.enableHooks).
- Improve templating helpers to produce deterministic hook/resource names and safe defaults.
change_summary: Schema tightening + templating hardening + optional hooks and init job to improve upgrade and rollback reliability for on-prem/private installs.
notes_for_release_manager: This PR is backwards compatible for existing installs (defaults preserve previous behavior). If customers enable values.enableHooks they should schedule a maintenance window for upgrades that run DB snapshots. Recommend communicating hooks opt-in via release notes to private customers.
changelog_entry: charts/private: values schema added; init-job and optional upgrade/rollback hooks introduced (see README for opt-in instructions).
testing_instructions:
1) helm install ./charts/private -f examples/minimal-values.yaml --namespace redwood
2) helm upgrade with values enabling hooks and confirm pre-upgrade snapshot runs
3) helm rollback and confirm rollback-hook runs only when enabled
4) run scripts/validate-values-schema.sh against values.example.yaml
